A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AlphaZero scaling study. Their complete main texts, figures, equations, references and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across section and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original state-frequency analyses, temperature experiments, loss measurements, and Oware and Checkers training results, including the inverse-scaling curves in Figure 5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds the agent-specific ground-truth loss analysis in Appendix E and Figure 13A.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same AlphaZero procedure, three-hidden-layer MLPs, value and policy losses, and 300 MCTS steps per move. Expanded explanations do not introduce an algorithmic component or establish a change to training or inference.

E1.justification: Both study Connect Four, Pentago, Oware, Checkers and synthetic branching-tree games. The new ground-truth loss comparison uses existing Connect Four coverage; the added game descriptions document existing environments.

E2.justification: The comparisons across AlphaZero model sizes and the alternative-hyperparameter Oware suite are retained. Figure 13 uses the existing agent-size comparisons, and newly cited research is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds ground-truth loss evaluation using each agent's own state-frequency ordering alongside the collective ordering used in Figure 4B. The solver labels remain unchanged. This adds a limited evaluation variant without establishing revisions to existing training settings.

E4.justification: New Figure 13 compares ground-truth loss under agent-specific and pooled state distributions, examining sensitivity of the loss-versus-rank relationship to that choice. Existing temperature analyses, early/late-state comparisons, training trajectories and capture-difference analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 adds uncertainty bands to Figure 4A–B. Appendix E identifies the bands in Figures 4 and 13 as standard deviations across agents, geometric for logarithmic loss axes and arithmetic for linear axes. This expands uncertainty reporting without reporting increased run counts or new seeds.

E6.justification: Figure 13A adds ground-truth loss curves under each agent's own state ordering, retaining the broad advantage of larger models while showing different rank-dependent profiles. Figure 13B repeats Figure 4B. These are additional results under a different evaluation ordering, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix J adds a complete derivation of the ideal-game ranked frequency distribution and its inverse-rank bounds, equations 13–26, where v1 supplied an assertion and illustration. This substantially expands the formal support for the tree-structure argument. Section 2 also corrects the capacity relation from n = cN to n = N/c.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same central claims: Zipf-distributed states, temperature-linked scaling exponents, frequency-ordered loss reduction, and inverse scaling associated with frequent late-game states. Rewording and regrouping the contribution list do not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Appendix H develops the existing hypothetical inverse-scaling explanation, describing why small models might relearn early states while larger models remain trapped after plasticity loss. v2 also notes untested effects of MCTS parameters and attributes the largest Connect Four models' loss stagnation to approaching optimal play.

D1.justification: New Appendix B documents board sizes, move and termination rules, including the Oware 1000-turn draw cutoff. Section 4 explicitly states that 300 MCTS steps apply during training and inference, and Appendix E explains dataset aggregation. These are disclosures, not evidence of changed settings; code-access information is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Paquette et al. (2024) and Schaeffer et al. (2025), briefly discussing the latter's heavy-tailed task-success explanation. Appendix A expands discussion of previously cited AlphaZero scaling work. The central positioning relative to the quantization model remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes local wording and terminology edits, separates v1 Section 5 into Sections 5 and 6, and expands background and appendix explanations. Most existing paragraphs and the main narrative sequence remain recognizable, so the reorganization is limited.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 13, combining a new panel with a repeat of Figure 4B, and redraws Figure 4 with uncertainty shading and adjusted axes. Other retained figure images are unchanged, although some move or receive new numbers. Title, headings and page styling adopt the NeurIPS format.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through uncertainty bands, the agent-specific versus pooled loss comparison, and clearer environment documentation. Appendix J supplies formal support for a previously asserted toy-game property, while Appendix H makes the proposed mechanism more explicit. These are useful, limited gains: the empirical scope remains stable and the inverse-scaling mechanism remains hypothetical.
